title: CS1 programming labs with style-anomaly integrity review
summary: Students complete multiple weekly C++ labs in zyBooks with unlimited attempts and immediate tests. Instructors use style-anomaly and similarity scores, code histories, time-on-task, and follow-up discussion to investigate externally obtained or AI-generated solutions.

sources.title: Style Anomalies Can Suggest Cheating in CS1 Programs
sources.evidence_quote: Programming assignments typically contribute 15-25% of the course grade

assessment.summary: Complete four to seven C++ programming labs per week.
student_actions: Write and repeatedly submit C++ programs.
Follow the coding style and constructs taught in the course.
Explain work if an instructor identifies a high-concern submission.

outputs.artifact: C++ lab programs and development histories

student_role.description: Externally obtained solutions, including ChatGPT code, were treated as possible cheating; style review was an instructor-side integrity control.

grading.method: zyBooks awarded 1-2 points per passed test with immediate feedback and unlimited attempts.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.

reported_results: Six labs from 2021-22 and three Spring 2023 labs were analyzed; style was a primary reason in 19 of 26 recent sanctions.

evidence_excerpts.quote: Programming assignments typically contribute 15-25% of the course grade
